scope: Scenario-aware calibration matrix for the single primary FX micromarket model.
ingestion_method: Semi-automated pypdf extraction plus hand-curated scale-matched proxies where the available literature is not directly in model units.

calibration_scenarios.name: baseline_primary
calibration_scenarios.description: Primary baseline without explicit exogenous shock.

calibration_scenarios.name: funding_liquidity_shock
calibration_scenarios.description: Funding-liquidity stress scenario for propagation metrics.

calibration_scenarios.name: snb_floor_removal_2015
calibration_scenarios.description: Removal of the Swiss franc floor on 15 January 2015. The repricing is pinned by the ECB daily reference rate, which moved from 1.2010 to 1.0280; the dislocation around it is an outcome of the model and is checked against the crisis targets of Breedon, Chen, Ranaldo and Vause.

targets.source: CME Group, primary FX liquidity on EBS (2024); Lallouache and Abergel, Tick size reduction and price clustering in a FX order book, arXiv 1307.5440
targets.market_scope: EUR/USD on the primary interdealer venue, which for this pair is EBS. The model has no intraday session cycle, so it represents one homogeneous liquidity regime and not an average over the day.
targets.statistic: median quoted spread in normal conditions, in bps of the reference price; price-grid diagnostic
targets.source_excerpt: Top of Book spreads witnessed a significant 30% reduction, Average Top of Book stands at 0.63 pips throughout the day. ... Over 20% of EUR/USD volume is now being traded on quarter and three-quarter pip increments.
targets.ingestion_note: REVISED 2026-08-15. This median was formerly identical to one price tick at every grid tested, from two basis points down to nine hundredths, and the book sat on exactly one tick in about nine periods in ten, so it measured the grid and not the market. It is no longer degenerate: the median now stands at nine to thirteen ticks. The band is kept as a diagnostic with low confidence because no source publishes a median top-of-book spread for this venue.

targets.market_scope: dealer intermediated limit order book depth around the mid
targets.statistic: smaller of the two sides of the book within twenty five basis points of the mid, averaged over the run
targets.ingestion_note: REPORTED ONLY, AND RENAMED 2026-08-23. Three things were wrong with this record. It was called near_touch_depth and described as one sided depth at the best bid and ask, while the series behind it is the smaller side within twenty five basis points of the mid, a band of some twenty seven pips: the realised value near four hundred base units is that band and not the touch, which stands at single digits. It cited a study of ASX equities, a different asset class with no designated market makers, for a foreign exchange observable, and a reader of this matrix saw that citation beside an FX target. There is no published EBS depth statistic identified for it, so the source now says so. What is available is a scale: EBS Spot average daily notional of 55.8 billion dollars over 86,400 seconds against the model's realised 0.456 base units per second puts one base unit near 1.3 million euro, which is close to the one million minimum trade size EBS enforces. On that scale the touch holds a few million euro, which is the right order for this venue. The quantity carries no band and no weight until a published depth statistic is identified for it.

targets.market_scope: EUR/USD high-trading-density signed order flow and CLOB-facing persistence
targets.statistic: lag-1 autocorrelation of non-zero signed CLOB-side order flow
targets.source_excerpt: Table D.1 ... EUR/USD ... the statistics in column (ii) test for the presence of (residual) serial correlation in the price changes, order flow and bid-ask spread process.
targets.ingestion_note: Switched from raw CLOB-flow imbalance rho to signed non-zero CLOB flow rho. The new band enforces small-but-material positive serial dependence consistent with high-trading-density EUR/USD and not the old 0.10 ± 0.10 convenience proxy.

targets.statistic: mean run length of non-zero signed CLOB-side order flow
targets.source_excerpt: Table D.1 documents non-zero EUR/USD order-flow serial dependence in high trading density windows, motivating short same-sign run clustering and not iid flow signs.
targets.ingestion_note: Diagnostic only: this companion metric checks short parent-order clustering so the calibration does not rely exclusively on lag-1 autocorrelation. The band is a modest one and rules out both iid signs and unrealistically long toxic meta-order runs.

targets.statistic: impact of a medium trade bucket expressed in model units
targets.source_excerpt: The average magnitude of the significant c1 corresponding to a price impact roughly ranges from 20 to 72 basis points per $1 billion in the order flow.
targets.ingestion_note: REPORTED ONLY. The paper expresses impact per $1 billion, while the simulator statistic uses a model trade-size bucket with no predeclared notional conversion. The former 0.5 bps anchor has therefore been removed and not retained as a zero-weight pseudo-target.

targets.statistic: share of dealers withdrawn during the shock window
targets.source_excerpt: At times when dealers' intermediation capacity is constrained the cost of liquidity provision increases disproportionately relative to dealer-intermediated volume.
targets.ingestion_note: REPORTED ONLY. The former 0.30 anchor was circular because it was re-anchored on earlier simulator output, while the BIS evidence establishes the economic direction but not a dealer-exit share for a comparable episode. The numerical target and tolerance have been removed. Identification is now through a separate 300-seed mechanism audit: low calm false-positive frequency, high crisis activation, wide separation of their confidence bounds, no scripted crisis pause, and no full dealer evacuation. Evaluated on the identified March 2020 episode from 21.08.2026. The synthetic dealer crisis preset it replaced evacuated the whole dealer sector on every seed, which is a scripted outcome and not an endogenous one.

targets.market_scope: funding stress propagation to spreads and depth
targets.statistic: correlation proxy between funding stress and quoted spread
targets.source_excerpt: Overall, our explanatory variables capture an appreciable fraction of the monthly time series variation in market wide liquidity of around 20%.
targets.ingestion_note: REPORTED ONLY. Banti and Phylaktis report regression explanatory power for monthly market-wide FX liquidity, not this contemporaneous correlation inside a shocked scenario. Neither 0.4 nor sqrt(0.20) is a valid target for this observable, so the numerical anchor and tolerance have been removed. The separately defined sign target retains the restriction the literature actually supports.
targets.known_limitation: The model's funding-spread comovement is high because the scenario moves funding costs by design. Its magnitude is a model diagnostic, not an empirical match.

targets.market_scope: direction of funding stress transmission to FX transaction costs
targets.statistic: sign of the correlation between funding cost and quoted spread

accepted_error_band.qualitative: sign must match the published direction

targets.source_excerpt: Our results show that (i) funding liquidity constraints measured by the availability of outstanding repos reduce FX market liquidity, and their impact is stronger when they are associated with an increase in the costs of funding and a shortening of their maturity
targets.ingestion_note: Demoted from a gate to a diagnostic on 16.08.2026 after its power was measured and not assumed. The direction is established in the literature, but this model cannot fail the restriction. Setting mm_alpha2 to zero leaves the measured correlation at +0.80, and setting it to -200, ten times the calibrated magnitude with the opposite sign, still leaves it at +0.18 and passing. Funding stress in this scenario arrives together with higher volatility and a cancellation wave, and those channels widen the spread on their own, so the sign of the correlation carries no information about the funding coefficient. A gate that cannot fail does not belong in an acceptance set whose purpose is falsifiability. The magnitude remains reported as funding_liquidity_stress_propagation.

targets.market_scope: share of routed flow executed on AMMs
targets.statistic: aggregate successful customer volume routed to AMMs divided by aggregate successful routed customer volume
targets.source_excerpt: Despite this restricted strategy space for liquidity provision, AMMs have experienced significant growth in trading share since 2020.
targets.ingestion_note: REPORTED ONLY. The source supports AMM growth and coexistence, but does not identify a numerical share for the modelled FX/EBS market. The former point target and tolerance have been removed. amm_share_pct is therefore only a weak routing prior under liquidity_aware choice. The reported estimand is a ratio of aggregate successful customer volumes, not an unweighted average of per-second shares with inactive seconds coded as zero. Arbitrage flow is reported separately because it is not customer routing.

targets.statistic: reserve scale, fee bands, and basis persistence plausibility
targets.source_excerpt: Trading in the FX market reached an all-time high of $5.3 trillion per day in April 2013 ... spot trading almost reached the same volume as FX swaps at $2.05 trillion per day.
targets.ingestion_note: WITHDRAWN FROM GATING 2026-08-10. The cited FX turnover survey contains no AMM reserve, fee or amplification estimates. These bounds remain useful engineering checks, but calling them literature-calibrated acceptance criteria would overstate the source. They therefore carry no objective weight and do not determine acceptance.

targets.source: ECB Foreign Exchange Contact Group, CME/LSEG presentation, 25 June 2026, slide 5
targets.statistic: Kaplan-Meier median lifetime of dealer-owned limit orders, in seconds, with live end-of-window orders treated as right-censored
targets.source_excerpt: Median order lifetime (sec) ... Bank ... EBS Market 290.
targets.ingestion_note: REVISED 2026-08-11 AFTER LIFECYCLE AND CENSORING AUDIT. The ECB-hosted CME/LSEG presentation directly reports the bank median on EBS. One model tick is one second. Each quote now receives an independent geometric cancellation clock whose configured 290 seconds is a distributional median, not a deterministic cap or an accepted result. Fills, stale-price amendments and withdrawals also terminate orders. The simulation statistic is the Kaplan-Meier median, retaining live orders at the finite window boundary as right-censored exposure; the completed-only median remains reported as a bias diagnostic. On development seed 42, the t=999 KM estimate was 259.0 seconds and the same early cohort's fully matured empirical median at t=4999 was 259.5 seconds. Structural gates separately reject lifecycle point masses, synchronized cancellation pulses and uncategorized endings.

targets.source: ECB Foreign Exchange Contact Group, CME/LSEG presentation, 25 June 2026, slide 5
targets.statistic: Kaplan-Meier median lifetime of fast non-bank limit orders, in seconds, with live end-of-window orders treated as right-censored
targets.source_excerpt: Median order lifetime (sec) ... Non-Bank ... EBS Market 2.95.
targets.ingestion_note: The model maps one tick to one second and estimates the lifetime median with the same right-censoring rule used for bank quotes. Independent per-order clocks replace the former provider-wide refresh cycle. This is a separate gate from bank order life, so the bank calibration cannot be obtained by relabelling all providers as slow; atom and synchronization checks also prevent a configured three-second clock from passing through a bulk cancellation pulse.

targets.source: Breedon, Chen, Ranaldo and Vause, Bank of England Staff Working Paper 711 (2018), Table 1
targets.market_scope: executed passive volume on EBS Market in EUR/CHF before 15 January 2015, bank versus professional trading firm
targets.statistic: bank-dealer share of executed passive CLOB volume, up to the repricing
targets.source_excerpt: EUR/CHF liquidity provider shares of trade volume in the pre-event period: human 38.8 per cent, bank AI 54.1, PTC AI 7.1.
targets.ingestion_note: EBS Market is interdealer, so its human traders are bank dealers and the bank share of provided liquidity is 38.8 plus 54.1, or 92.9 per cent, against 7.1 for the professional trading firms. This replaces the derived figure of 0.726 the primary pair carries, which was assembled from two venue statistics; here the share is measured directly on the pair. SCOPE CHANGED ON THIS BRANCH. Table 1 reports two days, the period before the event and the event day, and both rows are now read off the episode run, one from each side of the repricing, in place of reading this one off a separate shockless scenario. The two figures are then produced the same way on the same seed, as the study produces them on the same venue. MAPPING EXTENDED ON THIS BRANCH. n_fast_lp and fast_lp_base_qty both reach one, their floor while the participant exists, at a bank share of about 0.83, so neither can carry the pair the rest of the way to 0.929. fast_lp_base_withdraw_prob is added to the mapping as the continuous form of the same quantity: it is how often the one remaining non-bank provider is away, and it stands in for a sector this pair barely has.

targets.source: CME Group 2024 annual report, EBS Spot average daily notional volume
targets.market_scope: all EBS Spot pairs; conservative upper bound for the modelled EUR/USD segment
targets.statistic: executed model base units per second, with one unit approximately EUR 1 million
targets.source_excerpt: EBS Spot average daily notional volume was $55.8 billion in 2024.
targets.ingestion_note: REPORTED ONLY. Dividing all-pair EBS Spot ADNV by 86,400 seconds gives context of about 0.65 million currency units per second, but the source mixes all pairs and the model omits the intraday activity cycle. The former 0.10 lower edge was an engineering choice, not a literature estimate, so the range and pass/fail label have been removed.

targets.source: Breedon, Chen, Ranaldo and Vause, Bank of England Staff Working Paper 711 (2018), Table 3; Mancini, Ranaldo and Wrampelmeyer (2013), Table 2; and Huang, Ranaldo, Schrimpf and Somogyi, Constrained Liquidity Provision in Currency Markets, Table G.2 of the working paper (BIS Working Papers No 1073)
targets.market_scope: EUR/CHF on EBS Market: the pre-event window of 5-14 January 2015 for the lower bound, the 2007-2008 sample for the upper, and calendar 2016 for the third reading
targets.statistic: mean quoted spread, in bps of the reference price
targets.source_excerpt: For EUR/CHF, median effective spreads were 0.21 basis points for every trader type in the pre-event period. The same pair shows a median bid-ask spread of 1.80 basis points over 2007 and 2008. Its mean relative bid-ask spread on EBS over calendar 2016 is 1.71 basis points, against 1.01 for EUR/USD in the same table.
targets.ingestion_note: The two readings available for this pair on this venue each fail on a different side, so the target is the interval they bracket and not a point inside it. The lower bound is Breedon: a pre-event median effective spread of 0.21 bps scaled by 4.86, the effective-to-quoted ratio the same pair shows in Mancini Table 2 where a median effective cost of 0.37 stands against a median bid-ask spread of 1.80. That reading is in the right era, under the decimal pip increment this calibration assumes, but it needs a conversion taken from another sample. The upper bound is Mancini directly: a quoted spread measured without any conversion, but over 2007 and 2008, when EBS quoted in whole pips and a spread could not compress below one, so it overstates what the pair shows under decimal pricing. An earlier version of this target gated on the converted point alone, which made the conversion load bearing; the interval keeps the gate while removing that dependence, since it holds whichever of the two readings is nearer the truth. The tolerance is set to zero because the interval already carries the uncertainty the tolerance used to. THIRD READING ADDED ON THIS BRANCH. Huang, Ranaldo, Schrimpf and Somogyi report a mean relative bid-ask spread for EUR/CHF on EBS of 1.71 bps over calendar 2016, measured directly and needing no conversion, against 1.01 for EUR/USD in the same table. It is not made a bound, because it lands inside the interval already in force and because its year is the wrong one: 2016 is a year of free float. What it settles is the objection that the interval is too wide to constrain anything. Both direct readings of this pair, one from the whole-pip era and one from a decimal year, sit at 1.7 to 1.8, and only the converted reading sits at 1.02. The interval is therefore not an admission of ignorance about the level; it is the distance between a pegged regime and a floating one, and the model is calibrated to the pegged one, which is where the pre-event window of the episode lies. That the model lands at the lower bound is the expected place for it and not a residual of fitting.

targets.source: Chaboud, Chiquoine, Hjalmarsson and Vega, Rise of the Machines: Algorithmic Trading in the Foreign Exchange Market, Journal of Finance 69(5), 2014; Mancini, Ranaldo and Wrampelmeyer, Journal of Finance 68(5), 2013
targets.market_scope: EUR/USD on EBS, one model period is one second
targets.statistic: periods for the absolute distance between the traded mid and the latent value to fall to half its size at the shock
targets.source_excerpt: Algorithmic traders ... contribute to price discovery in the major currency pairs on EBS.
targets.ingestion_note: ADDED 2026-08-15. This is a structural requirement, not a fitted statistic, and it is marked low confidence for that reason: no source publishes a half-life for the convergence of a quoted mid onto a latent value, and the literature cited supports the order of magnitude and not the number. One model period is one second, and price discovery in the largest currency pair on its primary venue is a phenomenon of seconds. A band of thirty periods either side of thirty therefore admits anything that converges inside a minute and refuses anything that does not. It exists because the target set had no gate that could see a book disconnected from the fundamental. Measured before it was added, the model sat two hundred and eighty basis points away from the latent value a hundred periods after a three per cent repricing, closing thirteen per cent of the gap in three hundred periods, and passed every other acceptance target while doing so. The cause was that no participant in the book quoted off the fundamental: the book fundamentalists were set to zero and the price was carried by an anonymous scaffold with no owner. This target is what would have caught that, and it is what now disciplines the number of them. Evaluated on the identified March 2020 episode from 21.08.2026. The synthetic dealer crisis preset it replaced evacuated the whole dealer sector on every seed, which is a scripted outcome and not an endogenous one. DEMOTED ON THIS BRANCH. The half-life of 30 seconds is measured on EUR/USD and no EUR/CHF estimate was found, so carrying it as a gate would test this pair against another one. It is retained as a reported diagnostic.

targets.source: Breedon, Chen, Ranaldo and Vause, Judgement Day: algorithmic trading around the Swiss franc cap removal, Bank of England Staff Working Paper 711 (2018), Tables 1 and 3; effective-to-quoted ratio from Mancini, Ranaldo and Wrampelmeyer Table 2
targets.market_scope: EUR/CHF on EBS Market, 15 January 2015, the day the floor was removed
targets.statistic: mean quoted spread over the episode divided by the mean over the calm scenario
targets.source_excerpt: Median effective spreads on the event day were 0.92 bps for human traders, 1.22 for bank AIs and 1.91 for PTC AIs, against 0.21 for every type before it.
targets.ingestion_note: The episode study reports median effective spreads of 0.21 bps for every trader type before the event and 0.92 to 1.91 on the day, a widening of 4.4 to 9.1 times. The gate asks the model to widen by at least the lower of those and sets no ceiling. Two conversions stand between the study and the model and each fails in the same direction. The study measures effective spreads on trades while the model reports the quoted spread at the touch, and in a dislocation trades print in the moments the book is there, so an effective widening understates a quoted one. The study also separates three trader types the model has one of, and the widest of them is the one the model most resembles once its dealer has withdrawn. A ceiling would therefore assert a precision neither conversion carries. What the floor does carry is the thing the primary pair lacks: without it the size of the shock is free, and a calibration that failed to dislocate at all would pass every remaining target.

targets.source: Breedon, Chen, Ranaldo and Vause, Bank of England Staff Working Paper 711 (2018), Table 1
targets.market_scope: executed passive volume on EBS Market in EUR/CHF on 15 January 2015 from the repricing onward, bank versus professional trading firm
targets.statistic: bank-dealer share of executed passive CLOB volume, from the repricing to the end of the run
targets.source_excerpt: EUR/CHF liquidity provider shares of trade volume on the event day: human 68.4 per cent, bank AI 25.1, PTC AI 6.5.
targets.ingestion_note: The bank share of provided liquidity is 68.4 plus 25.1, or 93.5 per cent, against 92.9 before the event: the sector that provided liquidity did not change size, it changed composition, as humans took over from the algorithms inside the banks. This is the second half of the crisis gate and it is what bounds the episode from above. The spread multiple bounds it from below and cannot be bounded from above, because the study measures effective spreads on trades printed inside the touch and the model reports the touch itself, so the two multiples differ by a factor that is unknown in a dislocation and that the model, having no execution inside its own quote, cannot produce. This target needs no conversion at all: the study reports a share of passive volume and the model measures a share of passive volume. A dislocation severe enough to evacuate the dealer sector fails it, which is the discipline a ceiling on the spread would have supplied had one been available. SCOPE CHANGED ON THIS BRANCH. It was measured over the whole run and is now measured from the repricing to the end of it, which is the event day the study reports. Whole-run it averaged the event day together with the days before it, and a gate written on the one was answered mostly by the other: the same run reads 0.898 whole, 0.865 on the event day and 0.926 before it. The response window of a hundred and fifty seconds, which every other crisis observable takes, is not used and is reported beside this figure instead. Over that window the model reads 0.975, outside the band: the model's single non-bank provider prices off a reference that leads the lagging book, so through a repricing it crosses and takes instead of resting, and its provided share falls to about one per cent where the market's fell only from 7.1 to 6.5. Sweeping how often that provider is present, across its whole range from never absent to absent two thirds of the time, moves the response-window figure from 0.996 to 0.975 and never into the band, so the miss is structural and not a failure to tune. Table 1 has no row for a hundred and fifty seconds of a day in any case.

withdrawn_targets.reason: The cited JRFM article is about return connectedness among automated-market-maker protocol tokens. It does not estimate a price wedge between an order book and an AMM, and therefore cannot support either the three to twenty-five basis point range or a strictly positive lower bound. The model metric remains available as a phase diagnostic, but no literature-calibrated acceptance claim is made until a directly comparable spot-FX or same-asset cross-venue source is identified.
withdrawn_targets.measured_before_withdrawal: 1.59 bps in the seed-42 baseline audit

withdrawn_targets.reason: The target of twenty ticks existed only because the tick had no definition. It mapped a literature half life of one to three seconds onto twenty ticks through the assertion that a tick aggregates several book events, which was an assumption standing in for a missing time contract. The price process has since been anchored, so a tick has a length, but that is not on its own a time contract for the whole model, and the measured statistic is not the statistic the source estimates either. Lo and Hall estimate the decay of an initial impulse through a vector autoregression on an Australian equity book under aggressive order and cancellation shocks. The metric here takes half of the realised peak after a dealer balance sheet crisis and requires three stable observations. Neither the scenario nor the statistic matches, so the target has been removed and not restated in new units. A micro resiliency test built to match the source, measured in seconds, belongs in its own experiment. The half life of the dealer crisis stays an internal diagnostic until a source exists for that regime.
withdrawn_targets.measured_before_withdrawal: 16, 3 and 7 ticks on three seeds, median 7

revision_history.change: Two targets changed status after the tick was given a definition and the statistics behind them were compared with their sources. near_touch_depth was demoted to a diagnostic, gating false and objective weight zero, because it is a quantity and not a duration, its source is an equity book with no designated market makers, and no conversion from a share count into simulator units was ever fixed. recovery_half_life_ticks was withdrawn outright, because its value of twenty ticks stood in for a missing time contract and the statistic measured here is not the statistic its source estimates. Neither change was made to improve a score. The suite passed its gates before and after, and the demoted target is reported and still fails.
revision_history.note_on_prior_registration: The design targets of the 2026-04-27 matrix were fixed in advance of the runs they judge. These two were changed afterwards and that is recorded here and not presented as part of the original registration.

revision_history.change: Retargeted from 1.5 to 2.5 bps to 0.4 to 0.8 bps.
revision_history.reason: The old band was taken from client routed execution while the order lifetime and book concentration anchors adopted at the same time are interdealer statistics from EBS. A market cannot be both layers at once. EBS was chosen because EUR/USD is its flagship pair and because the economics of the paper, dealers withdrawing and a funded backstop, live on the primary venue.
revision_history.enabling_fix: The quoted spread was not a function of any parameter before this. A floor of 0.01 price units on the half spread of the automated providers pinned the market at 2.00 bps at a numeraire of one hundred, and it sat just under the value the quoting rule produced at the calibrated coefficients, so it never showed itself. Lowering any quoting coefficient moved nothing. The floor is now half a tick, which is the constraint that actually exists.

revision_history.change: Removed from gating and given zero objective weight.
revision_history.reason: The target was re-anchored to the model's own output in June 2026, after the withdrawn share metric was changed to count scenario imposed pauses. Testing the model against a number taken from the model is circular. A check reported earlier today, that eight seeds out of eight fell inside the band, is withdrawn on the same ground.

revision_history.change: Confidence lowered to low, mean added as a reported diagnostic, tick provenance claim removed.
revision_history.reason: An external audit observed that the accepted median equals one model tick, so the band is largely satisfied by the grid, and that the source reports a mean while the gate checked a median. Both are now stated. The claim that EBS adopted half pip pricing in September 2012 was not supported by the work cited for it and has been withdrawn.

revision_history.change: funding_liquidity_stress_propagation demoted to a zero weight diagnostic and reanchored, and funding_spread_comovement_sign added as a gating target in its place. The old 0.4 came from a sentence about carry trade premia and was both the wrong statistic, an R squared read as a correlation, and the wrong pair of variables. No published figure measures a tick frequency funding to spread correlation under a controlled shock, so the magnitude is now reported and not gated, while the direction, which two independent studies establish, is gated. The demoted diagnostic still reports its realised value and the gap to the field estimate is recorded as a limitation.

The EBS spread gate was moved from the median to the mean so that the model statistic matches the average reported by CME. The median remains a zero-weight grid diagnostic. cross_venue_basis_bps was withdrawn because its cited JRFM paper studies returns of AMM protocol tokens and not a CLOB-AMM price wedge. amm_volume_share and fx_amm_parameter_sanity were demoted to zero-weight diagnostics because their sources support only qualitative coexistence or aggregate FX turnover, not the numerical values used here.
revision_history.score_policy: These changes follow source-statistic matching and were made without tuning model parameters to improve the acceptance score. The withdrawn and demoted observables remain reported where meaningful.

revision_history.change: Added completed dealer-order median lifetime as a zero-weight validation diagnostic and clarified that the 290-second parameter is a ceiling, not a matched median.
revision_history.reason: The audit found that mapping a published median directly to a maximum quote life hid the realised order-age discrepancy. The new observable exposes that discrepancy without tuning the model or promoting a secondary source to a gate.

revision_history.change: Promoted bank and non-bank completed order lifetimes to separate gates after locating the primary ECB-hosted source, added a bank maker-volume composition gate derived from two primary CME statistics, and added a seed-panel mechanism audit for endogenous dealer withdrawal.
revision_history.reason: The prior model could match a 290-second setting while real dealer orders lived eight seconds, and its non-bank firms supplied roughly three quarters of passive executions. Both were incompatible with the chosen EBS layer. The exit-share target remains non-gating because the literature does not identify a numerical share; the panel instead requires zero calm exit, no scripted pause, stress activation on at least 75 percent of seeds, and no full dealer evacuation.

revision_history.change: Removed numerical pass/fail labels from touch depth, impact, dealer exit share, funding-correlation magnitude and AMM flow share, while retaining their realised values as reported-only diagnostics. Replaced the impossible zero-calm-exit rule with Wilson-interval tests of a calm false-positive rate, crisis activation rate and conservative separation gap.
revision_history.reason: The cited evidence does not identify comparable numerical targets for those five observables. In a stochastic endogenous model, rare calm activation is possible; identification comes from strong separation between calm and crisis frequencies, not a claim that an event has exactly zero probability.
revision_history.score_policy: The stored 300-seed trajectories were reassessed without changing simulation parameters. Unsupported failed labels disappeared, while every externally supported EBS gate and every mechanism check remained binding.

revision_history.change: Moved aggregate EBS Spot volume per second to reported-only context and added direct primary URLs for the EBS spread, order-life, participant-composition and funding-liquidity evidence.
revision_history.reason: All-pair daily EBS volume divided by wall-clock seconds is not a comparable EUR/USD point target for a homogeneous-session model; its former lower bound was an engineering choice. It remains useful context but cannot validate calibration.

revision_history.change: Replaced provider-wide deterministic quote refreshes with independent per-order stochastic lifecycles; changed both EBS lifetime estimators to Kaplan-Meier medians with administrative right-censoring; added per-seed gates for two-sidedness, lifetime atoms, synchronized endings, reason coverage and lifecycle sample size; corrected the official CME 2024 URL.
revision_history.reason: A configured median or cap is not a validation statistic. The former bank result was an 85-90 percent point mass at exactly 290 seconds, while fast quotes could inherit a shared clock and disappear after one second. Completed-only medians were also biased downward in a finite window. A long-followup development cohort confirmed the Kaplan-Meier estimate against the fully matured empirical median within 0.5 seconds.
